messages:
maria: Heads up - after yesterday's FP8 rollout to canary we saw a per-token tail latency spike on long-context requests (~8k tokens). Median fine, but 95/99th up ~2x.

jason: Which kernel path is being selected? FP8 should be faster not slower.

maria: Kernel selection logs show we fell back to the 4-bit approximate GEMM for the first 12 layers (layers 0-11) on these traces. Not sure why. Counters: `kernel_choice=approx_gemm_4bit` increased from 3%->67% for that workload.

lee: Any KV cache differences? Large context + cache hits could change seq-len distribution inside kernels.

maria: Yes - cache hit rate is ~78% for these traces. We profiled per-token and here's a compact trace snapshot (per-token ms):
```
token_idx: 7134 | kv_lookup: 0.12 | dequant: 0.28 | matmul: 1.45 | softmax: 0.20 | memcpy: 0.30 | total: 2.55
token_idx: 7135 | kv_lookup: 0.11 | dequant: 0.29 | matmul: 1.60 | softmax: 0.21 | memcpy: 0.31 | total: 2.62
```
maria: For comparison, baseline FP16 path for same tokens: matmul ~0.85ms and total ~1.45ms.

sasha: That matmul jump looks like DBR (dequant/block-reshuffle) overhead plus mis-tuned block size for approx_gemm_4bit on this GPU. Any kernel counters?

maria: Added kernel counters to observability yesterday. We have `kernel_invocations` and `kernel_time_ms` per kernel name. Snapshot: 
``
approx_gemm_4bit: invocations=2643, total_ms=4230, avg_ms=1.60
fp8_gemm_opt: invocations=1120, total_ms=980, avg_ms=0.87
int8_gemm: invocations=230, total_ms=220, avg_ms=0.96
```

jason: avg_ms for approx_gemm_4bit is double fp8_gemm_opt -> clearly slower here. Why was it chosen? Check kernel selection policy: we pick approx_gemm_4bit when quant_profile.size < threshold OR calibration_confidence < 0.6.

lee: Did calibration_confidence drop on these models? We had a calibration job for the canary that used short sequences (<=512). For long-context runtime the calibration distributions diverge.

maria: Exactly. Calibration confidence for this model on canary was 0.42 during auto-profile stage. That flipped selection to 4-bit path.

sasha: So interplay: poor calibration -> choose 4-bit -> kernel slower for this hardware/seq-len -> per-token latency spike. Need to add a ranking that includes measured kernel_time_ms on production traces, not just calibration heuristics.

jason: Agreed. Also batching heuristics may amplify tail. Our continuous-batching waits up to 8ms for batch fill; when approx_gemm_4bit is slow, the tail tokens queue behind earlier tokens more and 95th gets worse.

maria: Proposed immediate mitigations: 1) Add a short-circuit in kernel selector: if observed avg kernel_time for chosen path > 1.2x best-known path for same model+seq-range, prefer alternative. 2) Re-run calibration with longer contexts and include KV-hit distributions. 3) Add a logging flag to mark 'kernel_mismatch' when calibration->selection leads to higher observed kernel time.

lee: For observability, we should surface per-token breakdown (kv_lookup, dequant, matmul, memcpy) in the Console for per-route dashboards. We already have token-level traces for a subset but not aggregated by kernel.

maria: I instrumented a small change that emits a `kernel_mismatch=true` event to tracing when avg_ms ratio >1.25 for 1 minute. Canary shows several events.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: route=/chat/long-context, model=rwd-7b-mix, regression=avg_token_latency +62% at 2026-03-15T14:28:46Z

jason: OK short-term rollback of auto-selection to prefer fp8_gemm_opt for routes with high KV hit rate (>60%) until we deploy the selector fix. Can we do that via rollout policy?

infra-bot: deploy-plan created: rollback-selector-canary -> env=canary -> target=5% traffic -> owner=jason -> eta=15m

maria: I'll follow up with a calibration job (long-seq + kv-sim) and a perf harness run to collect kernel_time by seq-range. Leaving notes: include 1) warmup for KV cache in perf harness; 2) measure memcpy tail vs matmul tail; 3) test batching delay impact by toggling continuous-batch timeout 2/5/8/12ms.

sasha: Longer-term: expand kernel selection features: perf-observed latency, model-version-specific kernel profiles, and a fallback grace period so we don't flip choices mid-stream. Also add automated canary tests that run long-context traces.

maria: Thanks. I'll post results + benchmark table when done. For now watching the rollback and adding dashboard panels for kernel_invocations/avg_ms per seq-range.

lee: Thx — I'll prioritize a perf-test to try approx_gemm_4bit with different block sizes and a custom memcpy path; maybe kernel is memory-bound at these seq lengths.

jason: Great work. Keep updates here. :thumbsup:
